correctness.rationale: The original conclusions are correct, but the supporting-line argument at t=m asserted a false unique contact: H_m is zero throughout [0,m]. The complete corrected RESULT.md in /workspace/repairs/4/ proves the boundary case separately. Independent reconstruction: the signed Bessel radial coordinate |X|^k/(sqrt(2) k), k=(alpha+2)/2, has dimension 2-1/k=2-2 mu, giving the known last-zero Beta(mu,1-mu) free law. Conditional on touching zero between the two observation times, the product of signs has zero expectation by the strong Markov property and symmetry; without a zero it is one. A reset likewise destroys sign correlation. In equilibrium, the unnormalized measure of elapsed age a in a cycle remaining free of resets through t is P(W>a+t) da/m, also for atomic clocks by length bias and the uniform position within the covering cycle. Combining gives the exact incomplete-beta integral, or E[H_t(W)]/m. For w>t, H_t'(w)=I_(1-t/w) increases strictly while for w<=t the function is zero. When t<m, the tangent at m lies strictly below the graph at every other w, including w<=t because H_t(m)<(m-t)H'_t(m); Jensen is strict for a nonconstant clock. At t=m a nonconstant positive W of mean m necessarily has mass above m, on which H_m>0, proving strictness despite the entire contact segment. For t>m there may be equality, e.g. W<=t almost surely. The variance is (1/(2T^2)) integral_0^T (T-t) C_W(t) dt, because the indicator covariance is C_W/4; strict comparison holds at each positive horizon by integrating over 0<t<min(m,T). For the mass, substituting u=a+t and v=a/u inside one reset interval w gives Jacobian u and integral (w^2/2) E[1-B] with B~Beta(mu,1-mu); Tonelli includes infinite second moments. This implies the stated finite-moment variance coefficient. For the heavy tail, scale a=tx; the tail equivalence at t(1+x) holds with uniform relative error over x>=0 as t increases. Interchange the Beta probability and the x integral to obtain E[(1-B)^(beta-1)]/(beta-1), evaluating to the displayed Q. Rescaling the variance integral at 1<beta<2 gives the factors (2-beta)(3-beta) by integration of (1-s)s^(1-beta). At beta=2, Q=1-mu, integral_0^T C_W(t)dt~c(1-mu)log(T)/m and integral_0^T tC_W(t)dt=O(T), giving the logarithmic coefficient. The Poisson case also checks independently: the correlation is E exp(-rt/(1-B)); after differentiating with respect to rt and using z=B/(1-B), its derivative is -exp(-rt)(rt)^(-mu)/Gamma(1-mu), the Gamma survival derivative with the correct boundary. No claim of a CLT is made from variance alone.

value.rationale: The sign observable gives a unit-free measure of memory and a directly linked cumulative occupation noise. Comparing clocks of the same mean removes mere rate tuning. A single deterministic clock attaining every lag minimum (and every finite-window variance minimum), together with exact dependence on the reset tail and a logarithmic boundary, is a useful sharp benchmark, not merely an evaluation of the prior free Beta law or a generic renewal correlation formula. The proof resolves genuine equality and moment-regime boundaries and specifies the effect of long externally reset cycles that may themselves contain sign changes.
residual_risks: It is a variance comparison, not a distributional limit or an optimization over state-dependent reset rules.
